question: After geography, competing-climate and near-lineage falsification, which orientation mechanisms remain compatible with the East-Asian Cirsium pattern, and which stronger causal stories are no longer supported?

axis_specificity_boundary.bio15_nearest_pair_direction: 2/4 positive in full9 and 2/3 positive in Japan7

direct_mechanism_anchors.experiment: natural nodding versus artificially held erect capitula
direct_mechanism_anchors.fitness_result: achene set 56.3±3.9% nodding versus 15.7±3.6% erect; RR about 3.59; n=30; F=59.1; P<0.01
direct_mechanism_anchors.mediator_results: water and UV-B reduced pollen viability; nodding/involucral architecture was interpreted as sheltering reproductive tissues from rain/UV exposure
direct_mechanism_anchors.pollinator_result: no detected pollinator preference between nodding and erect capitula
direct_mechanism_anchors.relevance: strongest direct external capitulum-level functional anchor for abiotic protection; not Cirsium and not an East-Asian historical transition test

direct_mechanism_anchors.experiment: natural downward versus artificially reoriented upward flowers with pollinator, rainwater/sunlight, pollen/stigma and reproductive-fitness assays
direct_mechanism_anchors.result: downward flowers retained greater pollen viability/stigma receptivity under exposure and showed higher effective pollination and seed/fruit performance
direct_mechanism_anchors.relevance: independent 2026 demonstration that orientation can integrate abiotic protection and pollination; non-Asteraceae morphology, therefore general mechanism plausibility only

static_pollinator_preference_only.reason: The closest Asteraceae manipulation shows a large achene benefit without detectable pollinator orientation preference, and the existing EAzami mechanism-reduction analysis could not reproduce the cross-study bundle with a static pollinator-only pathway.

rain_wetting_uv_protection.reason: Direct capitulum manipulation in Cremanthodium links nodding to pollen protection and achene fitness in a cool wet monsoonal setting. The East-Asian Cirsium state contrast points toward a cooler / higher-BIO15 present regime and survives coarse geography, making this mechanism directionally compatible, but BIO15 is not isolated as a unique axis and no Cirsium wetting-to-fitness experiment exists.

thermal_or_time_window_pollination.reason: Existing cross-scale EAzami/Azami evidence and the earlier mechanism-reduction analysis support scale/time dependence rather than one static visitation coefficient; current data do not identify this pathway as the historical cause.

integrated_abiotic_biotic_orientation_fu.reason: Independent manipulation systems show that orientation can affect abiotic protection and pollination simultaneously, so the two-pathway model is biologically realistic; focal East-Asian Cirsium mediator and fitness links remain missing.

precipitation_seasonality_as_unique_caus.reason: BIO15 loses all-LOO specificity after BIO1 and geography are conditioned, adds no held-out prediction, and nearest phylogenetic pairs are mixed.

one_recurring_historical_climate_trigger.reason: Only one orientation event is calendar/paleolocation evaluable and no tested coarse historical climate class survives the full uncertainty envelope.

supported_statement: External experiments make abiotic protection, especially rain/wetting and radiation protection, a biologically credible mechanism for downward floral orientation. EAzami shows that the East-Asian Cirsium orientation contrast occupies a compatible present climatic regime and is not a trivial coarse-geography artifact, but it does not isolate BIO15 or any single climate axis as the cause. The focal causal chain remains incomplete at orientation -> wetting/pollen/effective contact -> viable achene fitness in ancestry-matched Cirsium.
decisive_missing_link: direct ancestry-matched Cirsium orientation manipulation measuring wetting/rain exposure, pollen retention/viability, effective pollination and viable achene set
claim_ceiling: External mechanism experiments are priors/anchors, not evidence that Japanese or Taiwanese Cirsium evolved orientation for the same reason.
Present BIO15/BIO1 correspondence is not transition-time exposure.
The Cremanthodium achene-set ratio must not be transferred as a Cirsium effect size.
Mechanism plausibility is not adaptation or historical cause.
No additional correlated climate proxies are needed to claim more causal resolution from the current public panel.
